In JavaScript, a computed object key that is a non-string value is coerced to '[object Object]', so these become literal property names, not zod index signatures (zod has no index-signature syntax anyway). The schema thus requires a property literally named '[object Object]' typed as number, so safeParse on a normal token response (access_token + expiry_date etc.) fails in credential-sync mode, throwing 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' via the callers in CalendarService.ts. judged_text: The computed zod object keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' at module load, not catch-all index signatures, so the schema does not implement the commented intent. In sync mode the schema only validates a property literally named '[object Object]'; any real expiry field (e.g. expiry_date) is not type-checked, and unknown properties are stripped by zod default behavior rather than allowed, contradicting the 'Assume any property with a number is the expiry' / 'Allow other properties' comments.
